subject: Intercompany payout misallocation between AWS/GCP listings - action plan
messages:
From: Laura Chen <finance@nimblecloud.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Discrepancy: November payout split across seller entities (urgent)

Hi Soojin,

We pulled our November marketplace payout and noticed a material split of charges that should have been billed under our primary seller entity (NimbleCloud Solutions LLC) that instead shows up split ~60/40 between two internal entities on both AWS and GCP invoices. This is causing the VAT treatment and our accounts receivable to be incorrect (we've been double-billed for VAT and the VAT credit is now misaligned).

Attached is a small extract (invoice_202611_nimblecloud.csv) with the marketplace usage lines and the seller_id and ledger references. Key ledger ids: LDR-98431, LDR-98432.

Can Redwood triage whether this is a marketplace metering attribution issue or an internal seller-entity mapping change? We need:
- A clear root cause (mapping vs ingest duplication)
- If it is a Redwood-side allocation issue, a plan and ETA for re-issuance or credit and how VAT invoices will be corrected
- Any evidence we should upload (tax forms, company registry, invoices) to speed resolution

This is urgent for our month-end close — can you confirm next steps and point person?

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Director of Finance
NimbleCloud Solutions

Attachments: invoice_202611_nimblecloud.csv
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discrepancy: November payout split across seller entities (urgent)

Laura — thanks for the detailed note and the CSV extract. Really sorry for the hit to month-end. I’m owning the customer side of this and looping the payments and marketplace ops teams so we can do a coordinated MAP (mutual action plan).

High-level next steps from Redwood:
1) Immediate triage (today) — Jonas to confirm whether the events were attributed to two seller_ids in ingestion or if the ledger routing changed during the billing window.
2) Evidence collection (by EOD Tue 2026-12-15) — NimbleCloud provides any seller tax docs and the full invoice for November (you provided a CSV extract; full invoice would help).
3) Remediation plan (Wed 2026-12-16) — if this is an attribution issue, we will run a ledger reallocation and issue either a credit memo or a re-issued payout depending on the accounting path.
4) VAT treatment (Thu 2026-12-17) — coordinate VAT invoice adjustments and confirm how the credit will flow (gross vs net depending on your country rules).

I’ve attached a short MAP template (nimblecloud_map_request.pdf) and added HS ticket HS-45217 to track progress. Jonas — can you start with a mapping dump (seller_id -> marketplace_listing -> invoice lines) and post a short summary to the Drive link? Marissa — please flag whether we should place the November payout on hold or issue a routed credit.

Adding payments perspective — thanks Soojin and Laura. A couple quick operational notes:

- If we confirm this is a Redwood attribution error, our options are: 1) Run an internal ledger reallocation and issue a credit memo against December payouts; or 2) Re-issue a corrected November payout (faster cash, more manual accounting). We should pick one based on NimbleCloud preference and their accounting constraints.
- VAT: we will need the VAT registration information and the VAT invoices associated with the affected seller_id. If NimbleCloud requires a reissued VAT invoice, Legal & Tax must sign off; please include that ask in the MAP.
- Wire/payment routing: If we re-issue funds, we need to confirm the receiving entity's bank instructions and whether they accept an inter-company re-route.

For now I recommend placing a temporary hold on any November chargebacks until we confirm root cause — this reduces the chance of duplicate remediation.

Internal FYI to Jonas: please include a delta file (original vs post-realloc) so finance can apply the adjustment cleanly.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Discrepancy: November payout split across seller entities (urgent)

I pulled the ingestion and mapping data for the November billing window. Preliminary findings: 

- The usage events for LDR-98431/98432 were ingested twice due to an upstream router re-emit during 2026-11-18 03:12 UTC. One stream was attributed to seller_id SLR-449 (primary), the other to SLR-778 (secondary). Both events made it into the aggregation pipeline and were billed.
- AWS and GCP invoices reflect the same duplicate event set because the router re-emit hit both marketplace integrations.

Recommended remediation path (low risk):
1) Create a delta reallocation file removing duplicated events from SLR-778 and attributing them to SLR-449. I will generate marketplace_entity_mapping.xlsx and the delta by EOD Tue (2026-12-15).
2) Payments team issues a credit memo equal to the duplicated gross value and tags it to NimbleCloud AR so their VAT team can offset as needed. Alternatively, if they prefer cash, we can re-issue a corrected payout; Marissa please advise.
3) Tax: once reallocated, we will issue corrected VAT invoices for the affected lines. Legal needs to approve the invoice amendment language — I’ll queue that with Legal after you confirm preferred remediation.

I’ve uploaded an initial mapping and the event-level dump here: https://drive.redwood.company/sheets/marketplace-mapping-77812 (read-only link)

Notes for bookkeeping: include both the original invoice id and the reallocation id on the credit memo so that NimbleCloud’s ledger automation can reconcile automatically.

Jonas
Marketplace Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
